name: url-state
title: URL State
description: Router-agnostic URL state: one UrlStateAdapter shape over the query string (historyUrlState), a hash router's query (hashUrlState) or memory (memoryUrlState), and useUrlState to read and write it.
docs: An adapter is `{ read(), write(params, { replace }), subscribe(callback) }`. `historyUrlState()` edits `location.search` with `replaceState` or `pushState` and follows `popstate`; `hashUrlState()` edits the query inside `#/route?…` and keeps the route; `memoryUrlState(initial)` keeps it in memory and records `history`, for tests and server rendering. A write through an adapter notifies its own subscribers too. `const [params, setParams] = useUrlState(adapter)` reads it with `useSyncExternalStore` (empty on the server) and writes with `replace` unless told otherwise. Wrap your router's own API in the same shape to use it instead.
